lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Jonah's poster exists only on a tablet that will not turn on before the due date. What is lost, and what would a separate backup still provide?

FEEDBACK
The poster file on the tablet cannot be opened, so that only copy is unavailable for the due date. A paper printout or a second copy on a different device would still let Jonah hand the poster in. Saving the poster again on the same tablet is still one copy, so a tablet failure removes both saves.

WATCH FOR
A common mistake is to think that saving once, or renaming a file on the same device, keeps the work safe.

WORKED MODEL
Maya's speech is stored only on the laptop, and when that laptop is left on the bus the only copy is gone. A backup on a storage stick kept at home, or a printed copy in a folder, would still exist after the laptop was lost. Renaming the speech on the same laptop does not make a backup, because both names disappear with that one device. What is lost with a single copy is the work itself: the words cannot be opened or handed in from a missing device.
